It is built on Kimi Delta Attention (KDA), a hybrid linear attention mechanism, and Attention Residuals, with native visual understanding and a 1M-token context window. It is the world’s first open-source model in the 3-trillion-parameter class, designed for frontier intelligence scenarios including long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning.For complete benchmarks and case studies, see the technical blog. Kimi is currently working closely with inference partners and open-source maintainers to align technical details and ensure the model launches reli

Model: Kimi K3
Audit fact type: reasoning_behavior
Source-backed evidence: Kimi K3 offers a 1M-token context and uses flat pay-as-you-go pricing — there is no tiering by context length. Input (with separate rates for cache hits and misses) and output are billed at uniform per-token prices. See Kimi K3 pricing. How do I turn off Kimi K3's chain-of-thought? You can’t — K3 always thinks. If the reasoning takes too long, set reasoning_effort to low to reduce the reasoning effort. See Reasoning Effort.

Model: Kimi K3
Audit fact type: modalities
Source-backed evidence: What is Kimi K3's context window? Kimi K3 supports a context window of up to 1 million tokens, allowing it to keep more information in context over long conversations and complex tasks. Is Kimi K3 multimodal? Yes. Kimi K3 is a native multimodal model that can understand text, images, and video within the same model. This allows it to work with visual information such as screenshots, documents, and video alongside text.
Applicable surface: API and model behavior

embedding_text:
Model: Kimi K3
Audit fact type: safety_behavior
Source-backed evidence: he Kimi Code harness (it attains 73.7 with the Claude Code harness); GLM-5.2, Claude Opus 4.8, and Claude Fable 5 with the Claude Code harness; GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 Sol with the Codex harness. All models are evaluated at maximum reasoning effort, except GPT-5.5, which uses the "xhigh" setting. As the benchmark includes cybersecurity and safety-related tasks, we also disclose the fraction of refused or fallback tasks: Claude Fable 5 hit 13 fallbacks and 1 refusal out of 80 tasks; 10 refusals out of 80 tasks entered GPT-5.6 Sol's cyber guard; GPT-5.5 had 3 refusals out of 80 tasks. Agentic benchmarks OfficeQA Pro. Each test case provides the agent with the entire PDF corpus, with all PDFs rendered as images and no machine-readable text available. OfficeQA Pro and SpreadsheetBench 2. Kimi K3, GLM-5.2, Claude Opus 4.8, and Claude Fable 5 are evaluated with the Claude Code harness; GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 Sol are evaluated with the Codex harness.
